clue.text: Ungentlemanly type, even worse with a different leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, and here that letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a bastard is a nastier sort of rotter than the coward the answer names

explanation.surface: A cad is described, and then someone even more dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: The replacement first letter is not clued separately; the definition fixes it once the base word is found.
explanation.definitionFit: A dastard is an old word for a contemptible coward, the stock villain of melodrama and no gentleman.

clue.text: Renounce, as police personnel have

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Officers give up something, just as the police have done.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown is to refuse to acknowledge any connection, a formal rejection.

clue.text: Spiritual healer's not a proper one

parts.note: a sham is something not genuine
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A sceptic says the faith healer is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal figure believed to heal through contact with the spirit world.

clue.text: Philosophical concept analysed as rot, badly

indicators.note: analysed means broken down into parts, so the letters are taken apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dismissive critic examines a big idea and calls it poorly reasoned nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'analysed' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: The astral body is a theosophical idea of a subtle spiritual counterpart to the physical body.

clue.text: Sad it's gone? Not cool, Vlad's loincloth

indicators.note: gone says that piece is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
hot is the opposite of cool
Vlad is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Vlad is upset that his loincloth has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: Sad with its it (SA, sex appeal) gone leaves a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a long cloth wrapped around the waist and legs, worn by Hindu men in India.

clue.text: Stopped working as a model, you could say, getting thrown out

definitions.text: Stopped working as a model, you could say
definitions.meaning: first sense, playful: a model poses
second sense: removed from office or power

explanation.walkthrough: 'You could say' flags the made-up reading DE-POSED, undoing the posing a model does.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposed ruler has been ousted from the throne, so the word means thrown out of power.

clue.text: Germany's elitist group in China?

definitions.note: china here is crockery, a noun naming a set of dishes

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
an inner set is an exclusive clique

explanation.surface: A question about whether Germany's elite clique exists in China.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C dresses porcelain as the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner set is a matching collection of plates and dishes, typically made of china.

clue.text: Producer of Bond cutting introduction: it's rotten

indicators.note: cutting an introduction removes the first letter

parts.note: epoxy resin is an adhesive that produces a strong bond

explanation.surface: A James Bond film producer cuts the opening sequence, which is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond is the glued joint, not 007.
explanation.definitionFit: Poxy is British slang for worthless or rubbishy, so it means rotten.

clue.text: Talked about cheap American trailer

indicators.note: about places the first word around the second

parts.note: spoke means talked
low as in a low price

explanation.surface: People discussed an inexpensive caravan from the US.
explanation.walkthrough: A trailer here is one who trails behind, not a caravan; the word is the US equivalent of slowcoach.
explanation.definitionFit: A slowpoke is American slang for a person who lags behind everyone else.

clue.text: Collectors' vehicle

parts.note: suggests a car owned by collectors of art or stamps, but means the lorry driven by refuse collectors, the bin men

explanation.walkthrough: Collectors sounds like hobbyists; here they collect household rubbish, and in Britain their lorry has an old-fashioned name.
explanation.definitionFit: This British term names the council lorry that picks up household refuse.

clue.text: Very little time to look

parts.note: to scan is to look over quickly

explanation.surface: Someone has hardly any time to take a glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Scant means barely sufficient, as in scant attention, so it describes very little of something.

clue.text: Clear Number 10 not against being offensive

indicators.note: not tells us the word for against is not kept but has something else put in its place

parts.note: obvious means plain or clear to see
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Number 10 Downing Street is pointedly not against something offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number 10' looks like Downing Street but splits: X is the Roman ten, and the base word's V (versus, against) is replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious means extremely unpleasant or objectionable, which is what offensive behaviour is.

clue.text: I want a head sacked! Preposterous

indicators.note: sacked suggests the letters are ransacked and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone demands that a boss be fired, and another scoffs at the very suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation, so the answer is an exclamation of disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are scornful exclamations greeting a ridiculous proposal, the phrase usually said with heavy sarcasm.

clue.text: Grand piano, one in church, returned

indicators.note: in places the piano and one inside the reversed church letters
returned means the church abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
p is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A grand piano and one more are sent back to a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand piano' reads as one instrument, but 'Grand' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic describes something on a heroic, imposing scale, which is what grand means.

clue.text: Tory minister working over rising colleague in hurry

indicators.note: over has the minister's name spread over and around the other piece

parts.note: Michael Gove, Conservative cabinet minister

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a mate is a workmate or colleague
on as in switched on

explanation.surface: A Conservative minister working on behalf of an up-and-coming colleague in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal urging to be quick, so it means to hurry.

clue.text: Supporter of ex-PM (English not American), one who was recently deported

parts.note: Boris Johnson, former UK Prime Minister

indicators.note: English not American says the English letter stands where the American letter was in the word for supporter

parts.note: a backer supports a cause or candidate

explanation.surface: A political hint about a backer of Boris Johnson, with a sly transatlantic spelling note.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Becker, the German tennis champion, was deported from Britain in 2022 after serving part of a prison sentence for bankruptcy offences.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Wimbledon champion was removed from the UK after his release from jail, making him a recent deportee.

clue.text: See orders for repairing screens

indicators.note: repairing means putting back together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone checks the orders for fixing some screens.
explanation.definitionFit: Reredoses are ornamental panels standing behind a church altar, a kind of screen.

clue.text: Extreme nerd — one might pick you up on grammar at first, I'm afraid!

parts.note: an Uber is a ride-hailing car that collects passengers

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of grammar

parts.note: the first letter of grammar
eek is a cry of fright

explanation.surface: A pedant fears being caught out on a point of grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick you up' looks like correcting someone's grammar but refers to a car service.
explanation.definitionFit: Über is German for over or super, so this is a geek taken to the very top degree.

clue.text: Previously left at home in care of nurse

definitions.note: sinister once meant on the left side, the sense kept in heraldry

indicators.note: in the care of the nurse means held inside her word

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse in Britain
in means at home

explanation.surface: A patient used to be left at home under a nurse's watch.
explanation.walkthrough: A sister is a senior ward nurse in British hospitals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for left-handed gave the English one, and heraldry still uses it for the left side.

clue.text: Strong drink: another litre abused

indicators.note: another signals a different arrangement: the letters made into another word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone downs one more litre of hard liquor and suffers for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abused' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; the unusual signal is 'another'. Builder's tea is British slang for strong, sugary tea in a mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Builder's tea is very strong, stewed tea, so it is a strong drink though not an alcoholic one.

clue.text: Rob Lowe gutted after fare goes up

indicators.note: after places the outer pair after the reversed piece
goes up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: grub is slang for food, fare

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides, leaving just the outer letters

parts.note: Lowe with its middle removed keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Actor Rob Lowe is disappointed after the price of a ticket rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob Lowe' looks like the actor's name, but 'Rob' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgle is to break into a building and steal, so it means rob.

clue.text: Teacher is following — O God!

indicators.note: following places these words after the O

parts.note: sir is a schoolboy's name for a male teacher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pupil exclaims in despair as the teacher tracks him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O God!' reads as an oath, but the O is a letter and God the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the ancient Egyptian deity of the afterlife and the dead.

clue.text: Means for controlling weather, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be pronounced, giving a matching sound

parts.note: rain is an example of weather

explanation.surface: An inventor wonders about a device for controlling the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The online grid showed RAIN, a slip the setter confirmed; the definition calls for the controlling strap.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps a rider uses to steer a horse, hence any means of control.

clue.text: Dogmatic believers do eulogise insanely

indicators.note: insanely implies the letters are scrambled wildly

explanation.surface: Zealots heap extravagant praise on their cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideologues are adherents of a doctrine held rigidly and uncompromisingly.

clue.text: Big around end of November and what follows it

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size
ca is circa, around

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of November

parts.note: the last letter of November

explanation.surface: Something large lies around the end of November and comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet the letter after November is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the radio alphabet the word for O comes straight after the word for N, so it follows.

clue.text: Mounted enthusiastic female singer

indicators.note: mounted means climbed, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: avid means keen

explanation.surface: A keen woman vocalist gets up on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Criminal cross — it's nicer outside

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are corrupted into a wrong order

parts.note: X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: An angry crook finds things pleasanter out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like an instruction to put one piece around another, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrinsic means coming from without, not part of the essential nature, so external.

clue.text: Man recalled daughter featuring in Vogue

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole is read backwards
featuring in places the daughter inside the other word

parts.note: a rage is a craze, what is in vogue

explanation.surface: A man remembers his daughter appearing in the fashion magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vogue' with its capital looks like the magazine; it means fashion, as in 'all the rage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar is a common male first name, so it can stand for a man.

clue.text: People divided opinion at the end — are maybe right about society

indicators.note: about turns the word for right round the other way

parts.note: OK means correct or all right

indicators.note: maybe hints the letters might be arranged differently
at the end takes only the final letter of opinion

parts.note: the last letter of opinion

explanation.surface: Opinion is split at the finish, perhaps correct regarding society.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to a nation split since 1945 into North and South.
explanation.definitionFit: Koreans are a people split between two states on the peninsula, so they are a people divided.

clue.text: Forest keepers who play in Scotland

definitions.meaning: first sense: officials who patrol and look after woodland
second sense: ..., the Glasgow football club

explanation.walkthrough: 'Forest keepers' also hints at goalkeepers of Nottingham Forest, a football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is both the term for park wardens and the name of a famous Glasgow football team.
